_comment: Free-text questions of the kind a tradesperson types, with bindings the query text itself rules out. scripts/measure-query-fill.mjs builds its corpus from each tile's worked example, so every number in it is labelled, in field order, with no distractors -- which is why it reports zero wrong values while these reproduce. Each row asserts what a number must NOT become, because that is what the query text settles on its own; which tile ought to answer is a separate question this fixture deliberately does not take a position on.
_schema: rows[]: { query, tile, mustNotBind: { field: value }, why }
_experiment_not_taken: Dropping the same-family unit conversion in the unit-agreement phase (fill only on an EXACT unit match) takes the wrong bindings below from 2 to 1 and leaves measure-query-fill.mjs completely unchanged: 4,349 / 7,184 fields, 0 wrong. That reads as free, and it is not. The recovery corpus is built from worked examples, so every number in it carries the field's OWN unit and no same-family conversion is ever exercised -- the harness cannot see what removing it would cost, which is a reader writing 3 ft into a field measured in inches. Refusing that is a real capability loss neither harness measures. Recorded so the next attempt does not spend the experiment again, and does not mistake an unmeasured cost for no cost.

rows.query: wire size for a 50 amp circuit 90 feet away
rows.why: 90 is the run length in feet. Binding it to the conductor's insulation temperature rating is wrong and plausible: 90 C is a real rating, so an agent has nothing to notice.

rows.query: fall protection anchor for a 310 lb worker and 6 ft free fall
rows.why: 6 is the free-fall distance in feet. Bound to a headcount it sizes an anchorage for six workers.

rows.query: control joints for a 20x30 slab 4 inches thick
rows.why: 20 is a plan dimension with no unit; the thickness is written with one, four inches, in the same sentence.

rows.query: how many studs for a 40 ft wall 16 on center
rows.why: 480 inches is the 40 ft wall length converted into a stud-depth field. Feet and inches share a dimension; a wall and a stud do not share a meaning.

rows.query: how many 4x8 sheets for a 24 by 40 floor
rows.why: Eight inches converted to feet, into a field for the length of a sheet. No sheet is 0.67 ft long.
